notes.title: Kunitsu-Gami celebrates 500K players with 3 Mazo Talismans!
notes.content:
500,000 players have entered the hauntingly beautiful world of Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess, ever since its release on July 19! Thank you to everyone who picked up the game! 

As a token of our gratitude, we are gifting 3 Mazo Talismans that can be equipped by the protagonist, Soh: Jubilee, Dancing Crane, and Amaterasu, which is a collaboration with "Okami." These will be available to everyone playing the game, and everyone who purchases the game in the future!

Additionally, a series of behind the scenes video taking a closer look at the development of the game will be released starting today! The first video focuses on how the world of Kunitsu-Gami was created, merging analogue and digital technology together.

notes.title: Bunraku meets Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess - "Ceremony of the Deity"
notes.content:
As the launch for Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess draws near, we are announcing a new bunraku (Japanese puppet theatre) play called "Ceremony of the Deity: The Maiden's Destiny" in collaboration with the National Bunraku Theatre. Produced by bunraku artists and supervised by Japan's Living National Treasure, Kanjuro Kiritake, this performance serves as a prequel to the game's narrative.

Discover bunraku, a Japanese culture with a history of over 300 years, through the world of Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess where the puppets for the Maiden and Soh were crafted using traditional techniques. Combined with state-of-the-art technology, the puppets will dance against a CG backdrop of the game's world to evoke a new and enchanting performance. 

Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess launches on Steam on July 19. Demo available to try now.

Capcom & National Bunraku Theatre - Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess Special Bunraku Performance
[previewyoutube=124HrR-M0iQ;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Wot I Think: Okami HD
notes.content:
It’s easy to mock Capcom’s seemingly endless stream of reboots and re-releases, but if there’s one game in the publisher’s back catalogue that truly deserves to be reincarnated for the modern age, it’s Clover Studio’s Okami. While Clover itself has since faded into the mists of time (the remnants going on to form Bayonetta studio PlatinumGames), its ink-washed tale of Japanese sun gods and monstrous demons remains as bright and vibrant as ever, the last ten-odd years bouncing off wolf heroine Amaterasu’s gleaming fur almost as if they never happened. Sure, there are still a few wrinkles and matted tufts here and there, but whatever anti-aging stuff Capcom and Hexa-drive used here, I want it, and I want it now.

notes.title: Okami HD splashes onto PC
notes.content:
The list of games I feel I’ve dearly missed by skipping most consoles isn’t long, and it grows shorter all the time as classics are ported to PC. The latest venerated console game to come our way is Okami, Clover Studio’s 2006 game about a sun goddess incarnated as a wolf to save the land from darkness with her magical ink brush, launched last night. Now named Okami HD, it’s not majorly rebuilt but it is a bit prettier and hey it’s on PC so good, great, wonderful.

Oh, and you’ll get a snazzy Dota 2 courier skin too. (more…)
